texts.preamble: Manager Manoj Kumar Sandilya S/O Shri ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 October, 2025 Neutral Citation No. 2025:Mphc-Gwl:26988 1 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh At Gwalior Before Hon'Ble Shri Justice Amit Seth On The 27th Of October, 2025 Writ Petition No. 15529 of 2021 Manager Manoj Kumar Sandilya S/O Shri Ashok Kumar Sandilya Versus The State Of Madhya Pradesh And Others Appearance:
texts.facts: With the consent of parties, the matter is heard finally. 1. The instant writ petition filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India claims the following reliefs:- "i) That, the impugned order contained in Annexure P/1 and letter Annexure P/2 may kindly be [LEAKAGE_MASK] with all consequential effects and the respondents may kindly be directed to permit the petitioner to work in terms of agreement executed in the year of 2020 upto its effect i.e. upto 2023, in the interest of justice. ii) Cost of the petition be awarded or any other order or direction deemed fit in the circumstances of the case be issued in the favour of the petitioner." 2. Brief facts leading to filing of the instant writ petition are as under:- 2.1 The petitioner being a society registered under the Madhya Pradesh Society Registration Act, 2009 was allotted the work of supply o f NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 2 WP-15529-2021 Cooked Meals/Take Home Rations to 315 Aganwadi Centres situated in District Morena and as per the pleadings of the petition, the last contract which was awarded to the petitioner for the said work was valid for the period from the year 2020 upto 2023 and the petitioner herein, for due Manager Manoj Kumar Sandilya S/O Shri ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184506675/ 1 execution of the contract work in question had set up a Centralized Kitchen, which is also being used by the petitioner for the supply of Mid-Day Meals to various schools situated in District Morena. 3. During the currency of the contract of the petitioner for supply of nutritious food to various Aganwadi Centres situated in District Morena, the respondent No.2 issued a Notice Inviting Tender (NIT) dated 14.07.2021, inviting Expressions of Interest (EOI) from eligible Women Self-Help Groups registered with National Urban Livelihood Mission/State Urban Livelihood Mission for the last three years and operating Aadhaar-seeded bank accounts for the work of supply of nutritious food to 315 Aganwadi Centres situated in District Morena. 4. The aforesaid NIT was challenged by the petitioner in the instant writ petition on the ground that during the currency of its period of contract, the NIT could not have been issued and the petitioner is entitled to complete its full contract period. 5. Initially, the instant writ petition was entertained by this Court, and an interim order dated 18.08.2021 was passed whereby, status quo was directed to be maintained by the parties. By virtue of the interim order of status quo dated 18.08.2021 being in operation, the petitioner herein completed the period of contract effective till August, 2023 and the relief NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 3 WP-15529-2021 claimed by the petitioner in the instant writ petition stood worked out by virtue of the operation of the interim order dated 18.08.2021. 6. However, when the matter was taken up for consideration by this Court on 25.09.2025, the Court was inclined to dispose of the petition, as, by virtue of the pendency of the instant writ petition and the interim order being in operation, the petitioner continued to work even beyond the period of contract. Nevertheless, on the request of the learned counsel appearing for the petitioner, the matter was adjourned for 08.10.2025. 7. On 08.10.2025 also, the matter was adjourned at the request of the petitioner's counsel and in the interregnum, the petitioner had moved an application bearing I.A. No.12619/2025, which is an application for taking certain facts and documents on record and also IA. No.12969/2025 filed on 27.10.2025 seeking amendment in the writ petition whereby, an additional prayer was sought to be incorporated in the prayer clause i.e. a direction to the respondents for taking action for allotment of supply of mid-day meals (Ready-to-Eat Meals) under the Centralized Kitchen Scheme launched by the Central Government and adopted by the State Government in terms of the directions issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shagun Mahila Audhyogik Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others reported in (2011) 9 SCC 340. 8.
texts.arguments: The learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner submitted that in terms of the directions issued by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shagun Mahila Audhyogik Sahakari Sanstha Manager Manoj Kumar Sandilya S/O Shri ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184506675/ 2 Maryadit (supra) and with the enforcement of the National Food Security Act, 2013, the work of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 4 WP-15529-2021 supply of Take Home Rations/Nutritious Food or Ready-to-Eat food to Aganwadi Centres can only be undertaken through a Centralized Kitchen and the participation of the Self-Help Groups at the local level, where the concerned Aganwadi Centres are situated, is not permissible under the said framework. 9. The senior counsel appearing for the petitioner further submits that the issue in question has been elaborately dealt with by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shagun Mahila Audhyogik Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit (supra) and even though, the period of the contract for which the work was allotted to the petitioner had expired, yet, in future also, any advertisement for the said work can only be issued inviting participation from such entities who are owning or capable to operate a Centralized Kitchen, and the involvement of local Women Self-Help Groups at the local level is impermissible. Accordingly, he submits that the advertisements dated 14.07.2021 and 13.8.2021, impugned in the petition, deserves to be [LEAKAGE_MASK], and the relief claimed by the petitioner by way of amendment application deserves to be granted. He further submits that during the pendency of the petition, the contract of the petitioner for supply of Mid-Day Meals to the schools situated in District Morena has been renewed by the same committee which is also responsible for considering the renewal of the petitioner's contract for the purpose of supply of Ready-to-Eat Meals/Take Home Rations/Nutritious Food to the Aganwadi Centres. 10. On the other hand, the learned counsel appearing for the State opposes the writ petition and submits that the period of contract of the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 5 WP-15529-2021 petitioner stood expired in the year 2023. It was contended that the petitioner had continued to operate and execute the work in question beyond the contractual period solely by virtue of the interim order passed in the instant writ petition. Accordingly, it was urged that the petition deserves to be disposed of, as the petitioner is not entitled to any further relief. 11. By way of filing an application for amendment, the petitioner is trying to get the contract continued contrary to the circular dated 5.5.2021 (Annexure P/8). The petitioner herein has not challenged the validity of the circular dated 5.5.2021, which specifically supersedes the earlier circulars and provides that nutritious food to the Aganwadi Centres is to be provided through Women Self-Help Groups only who possess the necessary eligibility conditions. 1 2 . The petitioner is a society registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1976 and not a Self-Help Group and, therefore, is ineligible to continue with the work in question under the provisions of the circular dated 5.5.2021. Accordingly, the State counsel submitted that the relief claimed by the petitioner through amendment application deserves to be rejected and the petition deserves to the dismissed. It is evident from the record that the relief claimed by the petitioner in the writ petition i.e. permitting the petitioner to continue with the supply NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 6 WP-15529-2021 of Ready-to-Eat Meals to the Aganwadi Centers upto the year 2023, stood worked out by virtue of the interim order of status quo passed by this Court on 18.08.2021, in pursuance of which the petitioner continued to operate and execute the work in question even beyond the period of the contract. 16. The advertisements impugned in the instant writ petition could not be given effect to during the pendency of the proceedings owing to the operation of the interim order and therefore, the petitioner may not be entitled for any further indulgence in the instant writ petition. 17. Since learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner had moved an application seeking amendment in the relief clause and has sought for a direction to the State authorities to continue the work of supply of Take Home Rations/Ready-to- Eat Meals to the Aganwadi Centres through the Centralized Kitchen Scheme and had strenuously placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shagun Mahila Audhyogik Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit (supra), this Court proceeds to consider the said contentions advanced on behalf of the petitioner. Though the learned senior counsel appearing for the petitioner had made a specific statement that the judgment delivered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Shagun Mahila Audhyogik Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit (supra) has not been disturbed till date, however, this Court finds that the said contention of the petitioner may not be correct. 18. In similar circumstances, when the work of supplying Take Home Rations to the Aganwadi Centres in the State of Maharashtra was sought to be allotted through an NIT by incorporating such conditions resulting in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 7 WP-15529-2021 exclusion of self-help groups, the said issue travelled upto the Apex Court in the case of Vaishnorani Mahila Bachat Gat vs. State of Maharashta and others, (2019) 15 SCC 718. In the said case, the Apex court also considered its earlier judgment in Shagun Mahila Audhyogik Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit (supra). The relevant portion of the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of Vaishnorani Mahila Bachat Gat (supra) is reproduced below:- 1 4 . The recipes inter alia provided for mandatory micronutrient fortification and mandatory use of extrusion technology in preparation of meals, thus requiring factory- based production which is difficult at the level of Anganwadi Centres, "Protein content in the food can be increased by confined sources and among the available sources Soybean is the best source for who are vegetarian, now the question arises that milk can also be considered as one of the sources but protein content of Manager Manoj Kumar Sandilya S/O Shri ... vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 27 October, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184506675/ 4 19. The perusal of the extracted portion of the judgment by the Apex Court in the case of Vaishnorani Mahila Bachat Gat (supra) clearly indicates that the earlier judgment in the case of Shagun Mahila Audhyogik Sahakari Sanstha Maryadit (supra) has been diluted by the Apex Court in the said case, particularly in paragraph 30. Paragraphs 36 and 42 of the judgment in the case of Vaishnorani Mahila Bachat Gat (supra) along with other relevant portions quoted hereinabove also indicate that the supply of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:26988 17 WP-15529-2021 nutrition to the Aganwadi Centres has been directed to be decentralized and that self-help groups are to be engaged for the purpose of supplying supplementary nutrition/Take Home Rations to the Aganwadi Centres at the local level as per the policy of Central Government/State Government. 20. The Apex Court in the case of Vaishnorani Mahila Bachat Gat (supra) also held that it is open for the Central Government as well as the State Government to frame the policy vis-a-vis the supplementary nutrition under the ICDS scheme based on nutritional norms read with the Act of 2013.
